subject: SLO qualification: streaming throughput & reproducibility plan
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@chargely.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-12T15:03:00Z
Subject: SLO qualification: streaming throughput & reproducibility plan

Tom — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from the perf/SLO thread so we all have the same frame: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Business target: interactive checkout flows at Chargely (tokenized short responses) where end-to-end perceived latency is sub-350ms p95 under steady-state load.
- Scale target: sustained 120 requests/sec average for the busiest service tier, with burst concurrency up to 250 active streams.
- Streaming behavior: customers expect interleaved partial tokens (server-side streaming) with time-to-first-token (TTFT) being critical for UX.

Clarifications / measurement definitions we agreed to validate:
1) Latency metric: p95 of time between request receipt at Redwood gateway and first full token emitted (TTFT), plus p95 of final-token latency for completion. We'll report both.
2) Concurrency: active streaming sessions measured as sessions with at least one open socket during the sampling window.
3) Throughput: sustained RPS measured after warmup, using 10-minute measurement windows.
4) Streaming tail behavior: capture inter-token gaps > 50ms as part of the tail; we'll compute per-session max-gap and include in distribution.

Action items (proposed timeline):
- We will share a canonical prompt bundle and harness runbook (attached) by EOD today.
- You provide a representative production trace or a small CSV with request size distribution and typical user think-times (chargely_test_profile.csv). If you prefer, share an S3 URI and grant read permissions.
- Plan bench run window: week of 2028-01-22. Internal owners: Marissa (runs), Ben (infra), Dev (measurement scripts).

Attached: prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl, slo_requirements.xlsx (high-level targets). Also linking the harness docs in case you prefer Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-harness

Please confirm: is the TTFT + completion p95 split ok? Any objections to the 10-minute measurement windows and 3x warmup runs? Once you confirm, we’ll lock down the run config and schedule the run.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

--
Attachments: prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl (jsonl), slo_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@chargely.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: QA Team <qa@chargely.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-12T18:20:00Z
Subject: Re: SLO qualification: streaming throughput & reproducibility plan

Thanks Chloe — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing targets: 

- Concurrency calculation: we measure concurrent sessions per user agent. For the checkout flow, concurrency spikes during peak sale windows; the 250 burst figure is accurate as an upper bound, but the 120 RPS target is what we care about for steady-state.
- Dataset: happy to share a sanitized trace. Attaching a small sample (chargely_test_profile.csv) that contains size distribution and inter-request gaps.
- Warmup runs: do you recommend a KV-cache warmup pass for streaming models (we use a conversational prefix per session) before measurement windows?

On the measurement spec: agree with TTFT + completion p95 split. One ask: can you also include p99 reported for final-token latency? Our SLOs are sensitive to long tails during sales events.

If you can confirm the exact run_config we’ll aim to give you a two-hour maintenance window (off-peak) during 2028-01-24 to 2028-01-26 for the full reproduction run.

Tom
Tom Reed | Head of Platform | Chargely
tom.reed@chargely.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@chargely.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-12T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SLO qualification: streaming throughput & reproducibility plan

Tom — great, thanks for the sample. We pulled the CSV and did a quick sweep; next notes and the concrete run_config below.

Key updates based on your sample:
- We will include KV-cache warmups: 3 warmup passes per model variant with the same prefix distribution you use. Warmup traffic will run at 25% of target RPS for 5 minutes each to stabilize kernel paths.
- Measurement windows: 3x 10-minute windows separated by 5-minute cool-downs. For each window we’ll report: mean latency, p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and final-token, throughput (RPS), error rate, and per-session max inter-token-gap distribution.
- Reproducibility controls: canonical prompt ordering (prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl attached), fixed pseudo-random seed for any stochastic sampling behavior (seed=42 unless you request otherwise), and deterministic batching order where possible. We’ll version the run_config so we can re-run exact configs later.

Proposed run_config (excerpt):
- model_variant: open-llama-13b-q4
- concurrency_target: steady 120 RPS, burst up to 250 sessions
- warmup_passes: 3
- warmup_rate: 30 RPS (per worker)
- measurement_windows: 3 x 10 minutes
- seed: 42
- metrics_export: Prometheus + JSON artifacts (per-request logs)

We attached: harness_runbook.md and run_config.yaml. Please confirm we can access the S3 bucket with traces (or share an alternate path). If Chargely prefers we've got two options for the run:
A) Redwood executes in our dedicated lab and returns artifacts (recommended for tighter reproducibility).
B) We provide the harness and you run under your org account (we’ll provide a checklist to ensure identical env).

Next steps: please confirm (1) p99 inclusion for final-token, (2) preferred run option (A or B), and (3) the 2-hour maintenance window on 2028-01-24/25/26. Once you confirm we’ll lock resources.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: harness_runbook.md (md), run_config.yaml (yaml)

2) Tom to confirm the maintenance window date/time preference. We can run either 2028-01-24 02:00–04:00 UTC or 2028-01-25 03:00–05:00 UTC.
